name: north-south scrap metal fence seen from above as a band of overlapping sheet tops on a post line, tiles into a vertical line
label: wasteland_ruins/fence-v

surfaces.part: overlapping sheet tops on post line (whole band)

answer.evidence: The silhouette is a constant 10px wide for all 16 rows, a vertical strip that tiles. The column scans show only stacked colour bands (teal, brown, rust) from top to bottom. There is no front-edge line, no eave shadow, no ellipse and no south face. The object looks like a plan view of sheets along a post line, so it has no vertical front face of 3 or more rows. It also does not read as an open frame or rack with beams and a base. It matches the 'top-down slab (no front)' reference.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a narrow vertical band of overlapping sheet tops, and I could only judge it at a small size. Measured facts support it: 15 visible tones per full tile, against 9 for the hedge, 17 for the cheese stall and 20 for the roofed well. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills. 0% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline leans rust or brown rather than black, which matches the Beodeul habit of dark material-tone edges. By eye, the rusty, grey and orange sheets are separated by value with some per-sheet variation. The ramps look slightly shallower than the references' 5-6 steps (about 4 per material), but the tile carries as much visible information as the same-kind references. It would not look thinner or more sticker-like beside them.
